unit.name: Monkey D. Luffy
unit.summary: A high-cost ranged damage and control unit inspired by Luffy's rubber body, Gum-Gum Pistol, Haki mastery, and relentless captaincy. He launches elastic punches and can specialize in heavier blows, Conqueror's Haki control, or rapid multi-shot pressure.

actions.name: Gum-Gum Pistol
actions.summary: Luffy stretches and slingshots one arm as a ranged rubber punch.

actions.name: Conqueror's Haki Burst
actions.summary: Luffy releases a concentrated burst of Conqueror's Haki that incapacitates several nearby enemies.

abilities.name: Conqueror's Haki Burst
abilities.summary: Manually invoke the locked Haki Burst action to incapacitate a bounded group of nearby enemies.

paths.name: Elastic Arsenal
paths.summary: Invests in the force and reach of Luffy's elastic punches.

paths.name: Haki Mastery
paths.summary: Builds a bounded Conqueror's Haki control ability with longer incapacitation and shorter cooldown.

paths.name: Captain's Momentum
paths.summary: Improves attack cadence and turns Gum-Gum Pistol into a multi-shot pressure tool with target reveal.

nodes.name: Long Stretch
nodes.summary: Gum-Gum Pistol gains 6 world units of range.

nodes.name: Accelerated Punch
nodes.summary: Gum-Gum Pistol deals 2 additional hit points of damage.

nodes.name: Extreme Reach
nodes.summary: Gum-Gum Pistol gains a further 8 world units of range.

nodes.name: King Kong Impact
nodes.summary: Gum-Gum Pistol deals 4 additional hit points of damage, finishing the heavy-punch specialization.

nodes.name: Conqueror's Haki

nodes.name: Overwhelming Will

nodes.summary: Extends Conqueror's Haki Burst incapacitation by a further 0.5 seconds.

nodes.name: Supreme Conqueror
nodes.summary: Reduces Conqueror's Haki Burst cooldown by a further 3 seconds.

visuals.description: Visual presentation should identify Luffy with his straw hat, red vest, blue shorts, and recognizable pirate-captain silhouette without relying on visuals for mechanics.
Gum-Gum Pistol should visibly stretch Luffy's arm and show a fast elastic punch traveling toward the target.
Conqueror's Haki Burst should display a dark red or black pressure wave centered on Luffy.

animations.description: Luffy winds back, stretches one arm, and slingshots the fist toward the selected enemy.
Luffy braces and releases a short, forceful Haki pulse that radiates across the area.
Additional emitters and projectiles should visibly represent simultaneous elastic punches rather than changing projectile travel speed.

audio.description: Elastic snap followed by a strong blunt impact for Gum-Gum Pistol.
Low, forceful shockwave sound for Conqueror's Haki Burst.

uncheckedRules: Character fidelity and prose/mechanic agreement require review.
The consuming game must implement these mechanics.
Runtime reachability, numerical balance and enjoyable progression are not established.

findings.evidence: Haki Mastery tier 1 modifies the effect of the disabled Conqueror's Haki action before its ability or action is granted. Tier 2 then grants the ability and repeats the grant, violating the dependency-order rule and making tier 1 non-executable as written.
findings.change: Make tier 1 grant the native ability, and make tier 2 enable the action. Preserve tier 2's existing summary and remove the duplicate grant operation.

findings.evidence: The supplied diagnostic scenarios measure zero utility for Haki Mastery tier 1 because its duration modification does not affect an enabled action. This is a concrete reachability issue in the sampled builds, although the diagnostics are uncalibrated and do not establish universal uselessness.
findings.change: Addressed by changing tier 1 into the ability-grant prerequisite; the control action becomes available at tier 2.

findings.evidence: The supplied scenarios measure zero marginal utility for Haki Mastery tier 3's manual cooldown reduction. The evidence does not show that the sampled scenarios invoke the active ability often enough to observe the shorter cooldown.
findings.change: No edit proposed; retain the explicit cooldown progression because the mechanic is executable and the diagnostic does not establish that it is universally ineffective.

findings.evidence: The supplied scenarios measure zero marginal utility for Observation Mark. Reveal is an allowed effect, but the supplied observables do not measure reveal uptime or any downstream benefit.
findings.change: No edit proposed; retain the bounded reveal effect because it creates a supported targeting-information interaction not captured by the current scenarios.

uncertainties: The diagnostics are uncalibrated and do not measure reveal utility, manual ability usage frequency, character fidelity, or player preference.
The supplied source supports Conqueror's Haki as a control concept, but does not specify exact incapacitation duration, area, cooldown, or reliability; those remain design values.

limits: Source fidelity review remains model judgment. Diagnostics are uncalibrated mechanical evidence.
A rejected or failed review preserves the draft; structural success does not mean the review succeeded.
Only complete valid transactions are committed. Large redesigns and missing top-level structures may remain unrepaired.
Feasibility and source attribution remain model judgments. A supported claim in the plan is not an independent verification of the final implementation.

plan.identity: Public design specification and feasibility report: Monkey D. Luffy is represented as a high-cost, one-placement damage/control unit inspired by his rubber body, Gum-Gum Pistol, Haki, and characteristic combat progression. Purchase cost: 650 credits. Role profile: damage, burst, control. Base reach is 30 world units. The design is feasible under classic-three-path: three independent five-tier paths, one native active

baseAttack.description: Gum-Gum Pistol: Luffy stretches and slingshots his arm as a ranged punch. It is a single-target projectile attack with 30 world-unit range, 45 world-units-per-second travel speed, one projectile per cycle, 3 hit points of damage, and a 1.2-second recurring attack period.

paths.name: Elastic Arsenal
progression: Tier 1: increase Gum-Gum Pistol damage by 1 hit point.
Tier 2: increase Gum-Gum Pistol range by 6 world units.
Tier 3: increase Gum-Gum Pistol damage by 2 hit points.
Tier 4: increase Gum-Gum Pistol range by 8 world units.
Tier 5: increase Gum-Gum Pistol damage by 4 hit points.

paths.name: Haki Mastery
progression: Tier 1: unlock the Conqueror's Haki control effect for the later ability.
Tier 2: grant and enable the native active Conqueror's Haki Burst ability.
Tier 3: reduce Conqueror's Haki Burst cooldown by 2 seconds.
Tier 4: increase the Burst's incapacitation duration by 0.5 seconds.
Tier 5: reduce Conqueror's Haki Burst cooldown by a further 3 seconds.

paths.name: Captain's Momentum
progression: Tier 1: reduce Gum-Gum Pistol's recurring attack period by 0.15 seconds.
Tier 2: add one additional attack emitter.
Tier 3: add one additional projectile per cycle.
Tier 4: increase each projectile's collateral target cap by 1.
Tier 5: add target reveal to Gum-Gum Pistol hits.

mechanics.name: Conqueror's Haki
mechanics.implementation: A declared area control effect that applies an incapacitating status to eligible nearby targets for an explicit duration. Status resistance and immunity are supplied by game context; this mechanic does not invent universal knockout behavior.

mechanics.name: Conqueror's Haki Burst
mechanics.implementation: One manually invoked active ability, granted at Haki Mastery tier 2. It uses an area delivery with a finite radius and target cap, applies the declared Conqueror's Haki incapacitation status, and has an explicit cooldown. It is an attack/control adaptation, not a runtime transformation or generic self-stat modifier.

mechanics.name: Observation-inspired reveal
mechanics.implementation: At Captain's Momentum tier 5, Gum-Gum Pistol hits reveal targets for an explicit duration. This adapts Luffy's presence and movement detection into a supported target-reveal effect.

omissions.sourceTrait: Gear 2 as a temporary body transformation that increases strength and speed and imposes strain or energy costs.
omissions.reason: Runtime transformations and generic self-stat modifiers are unsupported. The design uses a shorter recurring attack period in Captain's Momentum as an honest attack-progression adaptation, not as a Gear 2 transformation.

omissions.sourceTrait: Gear 3's enlarged body parts, high-damage attacks, and original post-use shrinking drawback.
omissions.reason: The source distinction is retained but not implemented: runtime transformation, temporary reversion, and the stated shrink drawback cannot be represented safely under the encounter-form rules.

omissions.sourceTrait: Gear 4's inflated-muscle form, Armament Haki coating, compression attacks, and aerial propulsion.
omissions.reason: No runtime forms or generic body-stat transformations are declared. Its powerful-strike concept is only represented indirectly through damage progression, without claiming Gear 4 activation.

omissions.sourceTrait: Gear 5 as an awakened white-haired transformation with imagination-limited freedom and a specific awakening trigger.
omissions.reason: Forms are external encounter selections rather than runtime transformations, and the supplied contract does not support an encounter trigger based on suffering a fatal blow. No Gear 5 form is declared.

omissions.sourceTrait: Turning the environment and living beings into rubber.
omissions.reason: The supported effects do not provide a general environmental or arbitrary target transformation mechanic.

omissions.sourceTrait: Rubber immunity to electricity, blunt-force resistance, and vulnerability to sharp weapons.
omissions.reason: The default contract excludes generic stat modifiers and does not provide damage-type resistance or weakness fields.

omissions.sourceTrait: Loss of strength and independent movement in water or near Sea-Prism Stone.
omissions.reason: The unit contract has no supplied environmental weakness, suppression state, or Sea-Prism Stone interaction definition.

omissions.sourceTrait: Armament Haki defense, Devil Fruit negation, Emission, Internal Destruction, and Conqueror's Haki coating.
omissions.reason: The design selects only a supported control subset of Haki. Defense modifiers, negation, penetration, and attack-coating transformations lack directly supported properties in this draft.

omissions.sourceTrait: Future Sight seeing several seconds into the future.
omissions.reason: The supported reveal effect is a narrower Observation-inspired adaptation; predictive evasion or guaranteed future knowledge is not implemented.

omissions.sourceTrait: Poison immunity with slow susceptibility to strong poison.
omissions.reason: The contract does not define damage-type immunity or resistance fields, and no poison status context was supplied.

omissions.sourceTrait: Crew, Grand Fleet, family relationships, political affiliations, bounty progression, and narrative achievements.
omissions.reason: These establish identity and lore but do not map to an executable single-placement combat unit without additional roster, ally, economy, or narrative systems.

uncertainties: The supplied evidence does not specify exact attack damage, cooldowns, control reliability, or Haki ranges; the numeric values in this specification are design values, not source claims.
The control status requires the consuming game context to define its exact incapacitation semantics and resistance handling.

Projectile travel speed is fixed at 45 world units per second and is not upgraded. Captain's Momentum changes recurring attack period, emitter count, projectile count, collateral target cap, and reveal—not projectile travel speed.
No form is declared, so the design remains within the external-activation and encounter-persistence form rules.
The source is a secondary reference record and does not provide a complete catalog of named attacks, Gear 4 variants, Gear 5 applications, or Haki techniques.

effectiveLimits.prominentMechanicCounting: Every declared ability plus every declared form plus one if control is used plus one if damage-over-time is used. Locked declarations still count. Resources do not directly count, but their associated abilities and forms do.

forms.requirements: empty; grant-form upgrade or explicit external unlock

effectiveLimits.formLimitations: Forms are external encounter selections. They do not switch at runtime, revert, enforce mutually exclusive modes, or make arbitrary combinations safe. A grant-form upgrade unlocks a later external build selection.
effectiveLimits.intervalCadence: For an enabled primary interval action, scheduled period = max(trigger.intervalSeconds, timing.cooldownSeconds). A fixed trigger interval can mask cooldown upgrades. A trigger floor of 0.15 seconds allows cooldown upgrades down to that floor; use a different explicit interval only when intentional. Windup delays resolution separately.
effectiveLimits.delivery: Direct-strike and line-strike can have range up to the same configured maximum as projectiles. Melee does not imply short range. Projectile primary aim count and collateral pierce are separate; do not infer a combined minimum target cap.

projectileSpeed.implementation: A speed change needs a separately declared replacement action with a different projectileSpeedWorldUnitsPerSecond and a valid replace-action operation, or an honestly revised progression. Replacement must satisfy all existing reference, ownership and lifecycle rules.

parameterMeaning.cooldownSeconds: Time gate between action invocations; recurring scheduling also uses trigger.intervalSeconds.
parameterMeaning.emitterCount: Number of emitters, not travel speed.
parameterMeaning.projectilesPerCycle: Shots emitted per cycle, not projectile travel speed.
parameterMeaning.maximumTargetsPerProjectile: Collateral target/pierce limit, not projectile travel speed.
